title: Castlevania: Circle of the Moon
subtitle: A new handheld opens another castle
summary: Castlevania: Circle of the Moon is Konami's Game Boy Advance action role-playing adventure following vampire hunter Nathan Graves into Dracula's castle to rescue his mentor. Released alongside the handheld in Japan, it brings the interconnected exploration associated with Symphony of the Night into a smaller screen. Fighting enemies develops Nathan's abilities while new movement options open routes through the building. Its castle is a place to learn gradually, with the discovery of another useful ability changing the meaning of a corridor or obstacle encountered earlier in the journey.
body: Castlevania: Circle of the Moon is Konami's Game Boy Advance action role-playing adventure following vampire hunter Nathan Graves into Dracula's castle to rescue his mentor. Released alongside the handheld in Japan, it brings the interconnected exploration associated with Symphony of the Night into a smaller screen. Fighting enemies develops Nathan's abilities while new movement options open routes through the building. Its castle is a place to learn gradually, with the discovery of another useful ability changing the meaning of a corridor or obstacle encountered earlier in the journey.

The Dual Set-Up System combines cards associated with attributes and actions to produce magical effects. Finding a card therefore adds possibilities in relation to the collection already held, rather than supplying only one isolated ability. Different pairings can alter how Nathan attacks or responds to a difficult encounter. The system gives exploration another practical reward alongside equipment and experience. A newly discovered component may help with the immediate fight, but it can also make an older card useful in a combination that was previously unavailable to the player.

Progress through the castle depends on gaining abilities that make previously inaccessible places reachable. The map gradually becomes a record of both explored space and unfinished possibilities, encouraging the player to remember a passage that could not yet be crossed. Combat and character development support the same journey, providing the strength needed to explore further. Circle of the Moon connects those activities through its enclosed setting, making a return visit productive because Nathan may now possess a movement, an item or a card arrangement that changes what the earlier location allows.
